claims.claim_ar: بَيَانٌ مشتق من الجذر بين بمعنى الإظهار والتبيين/التفريق
claims.claim_en: The noun بَيَانٌ derives from the root ب-ي-ن meaning 'to make clear, to show, to distinguish', i.e. 'clarity/clarification'.

claims.claim_ar: بَيَانٌ على وزن فِعَال/فِعَالٍ (اسم يدل على الإظهار والبيان)، تصنيف الشكل الصرفي تقليدي
claims.claim_en: The pattern (wazn) of بَيَانٌ is commonly described as fi'āl (فِعَال), a nominal pattern producing abstract nouns of clarity/manifestation.
claims.needs_review_reason: Classical pattern labels vary; confirm exact morphological notation (fi'āl vs other transcription) against a dedicated sarf reference.

claims.claim_ar: المُتَّقِينَ من الجذر وقى بمعنى اتقاء/التقوى والخشية والحذر من معصية الله
claims.claim_en: The form المُتَّقِينَ is derived from the root و-ق-ي meaning 'to guard oneself; to fear/revere (God)'; hence المُتَّقُون are 'the pious, God-fearing/ those who observe taqwa'.
claims.needs_review_reason: Evidence cited is an inflected verbal form (تَتَّقُوا) from the commentary rather than the exact noun form in the ayah; confirm morphological derivation/labeling in a sarf dictionary.

warnings: Provided source chunks do not contain exact occurrences of several ayah words (e.g. 'هَذَا', 'هُدًى', 'مَوْعِظَةٌ', 'لِلنَّاسِ') so claims were produced only for words where a related substring / cognate form was present in the supplied commentary.

Some claims use related inflected forms from the commentary (e.g. 'بَيْنَ' inside 'لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهُمْ', 'تَتَّقُوا') as evidence for the root/meaning of the ayah-word; these are flagged in needs_review_reason where applicable.
